Overall: 8/10.

Story & Plot

Things initially seem to be going well for Bonnie and her toys until Bonnie receives a Lilypad tablet as a gift and becomes entirely obsessed with it. This creates an all-new threat to playtime, making the jobs of Buzz, Woody, Jessie, and the rest of the gang exponentially harder as they go head-to-head with the digital age. The narrative explores what true friendship means in a world dominated by online presence, contacts, and followers rather than real-life experiences.

Comedy & Entertainment

Toy Story 5 is celebrated by reviewers as possibly the funniest movie in the series, delivering plenty of laughs alongside its real-world emotions. A significant portion of this humor stems from new, weird additions to the toy lineup, including a potty-training device voiced by Conan O'Brien. His unique energy and strangeness are matched by returning characters like Forky—who is now married and still saying the wrong thing—contributing to a high level of entertainment value.

Performances & Direction

The voice cast delivers strong performances that anchor the emotional and comedic beats of the film. Tom Hanks, Tim Allen, and Joan Cusack return to their iconic roles, while Conan O'Brien brings exceptional comedic energy as a potty-training device. Additionally, the film finally puts the spotlight on the fearless cowgirl Jessie, grounding the emotional core with her dedicated character arc.

Strengths

  • Hilarious new additions to the cast
  • Conan O'Brien's standout comedic energy
  • Heartfelt exploration of the digital age
  • Visually stunning animation and play sequences
  • Jessie taking the spotlight

Weaknesses

Despite its moments of joy and beautiful animation, some reviewers note that the creative well feels somewhat dry. It can feel like an inconsequential entry that struggles to compare to the early peaks of the franchise, leading to a sense of a familiar setup for seasoned viewers.

Final verdict

Toy Story 5 successfully brings the beloved gang into the digital age while offering plenty of laughs and profound reflections on human connection. Backed by a stellar voice cast and a hilarious new addition in Conan O'Brien, it is well worth a watch for families and franchise fans alike. Recommended for those looking to see how classic toys handle modern technology.

Lust Stories 3 is a Hindi-language anthology film directed by Vikramaditya Motwane, featuring four bite-sized yet emotionally resonant segments. Through these chapters, the film explores lust, love, relationships, and repressed desire, offering fresh perspectives on intimacy and human connection. Reviewers note that it acts as a mirror to modern relationships, shedding past shock value for the disturbing terrain of emotional isolation.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film focuses heavily on provocation and the complexities of romance rather than traditional laughs or slapstick humor. Its entertainment value stems from its bold premise and attractively-wrapped pieces of provocation that examine modern intimacy. While some segments lean heavily on twists, the overall tone remains a sincere and engaging anthology.

Weaknesses

Despite its highlights, the anthology is ultimately uneven in its storytelling. Some reviewers point out that certain segments feel disappointingly predictable with characters that never become genuinely compelling, while other parts rely too heavily on their specific premise or twist.

Final verdict

Lust Stories 3 is an uneven but enjoyable anthology that successfully brings fresh perspectives to modern relationships and intimacy. Led by lively performances from a talented cast, it offers a bold exploration of love and repressed desire despite some predictable storytelling. It comes recommended for fans of the franchise looking for a provocative and engaging watch.
